study.name: Vennard House: The Study
study.recap: The study is as you left it. The shutters bang in the gale, and the sweet smell still clings to the room.

beats.n: You kneel beside the settee and lift the dinner coat.
Master Aldous Vennard looks younger than his sixty-three years. There is no blood, no bruise, no mark at all.
But his face has a colour you did not expect: a warm, healthy, cherry-pink flush, as if he had come in from the cold.

beats.t: "Dr. Brine will want to see that at the Watch House, Inspector. I've never seen a man of a seizure look so well."

objects.label: Inspect the locked door
objects.intro: You cross to the door and crouch by the lock.

objects.label: Examine the windows
objects.intro: You walk the room's edge, window by window.

objects.label: Examine the wall lamp bracket
objects.intro: You lift the lamp's chimney aside and look at the bracket behind it.

objects.label: Examine the gas lamp
objects.intro: The brass lamp beside the desk is cold now. You turn it in your hands.

objects.label: Search the desk
objects.intro: The big desk faces the wall lamp. A blotter, a pen, a half-finished page.

objects.label: Unlock the desk drawer
objects.intro: The small key from the watch-chain turns in the lower drawer.

objects.label: Examine the French window
objects.intro: You go to the French window at the end of the room.

beats.n: The grate is cold and swept. The damper is shut, and the ash lies undisturbed in the pan.
Nothing has come down this chimney tonight, and nothing has gone up it.

objects.label: Try the safe behind the north panel
Take the ledger page from the safe
Take the drawings from the safe
Read the contract in the safe

hall.name: Vennard House: Grand Hall & Conservatory
hall.recap: The Grand Hall waits, hushed and half-lit. The household are scattered through the rooms beyond.

objects.label: Examine the hired-staff list
objects.intro: On the steward's table lies the night's hire-book.

objects.label: Ask the guests about the toast, and Hob about the door
Ask the guests about Mr. Corvane
Ask Ned Bracken in the conservatory

stairs.name: Vennard House: Below Stairs
stairs.recap: The servants' hall is warm and full of murmuring. Everyone stops when you come in.

objects.label: Examine the key register in the pantry
objects.intro: In the pantry a slate hangs beside the key-board.

objects.label: Ask Nell and Hob about the study lamp
Examine the cellar tool board
objects.intro: You take a lantern down the cellar stair.

objects.label: Go up the back stair to Pell's room

pellsroom.name: Vennard House: Pell's Room
pellsroom.recap: A narrow room at the top of the back stair, squared to the edge of every piece of furniture.

emptyBeats.n: The washstand drawer is empty. Something has been taken out of it in a hurry, and lately: the dust is bright where it stood.
Under the bed, only a clean square on the boards. Whatever lay here has gone.
In the grate downstairs, you are told later, a butler was seen burning papers.

watch.name: Watch House, Halberd Street
watch.recap: The morgue keeps its own quiet, tiled and gaslit. Dr. Brine looks up as you come down the steps.

objects.label: Read the surgeon's report
objects.intro: Dr. Brine slides the report across the steel table.

objects.label: Ask Dr. Brine whether it could have been an accident

beatsFn.$fn: () => (has("C03") && has("C04")) ? [ { y: "Could it have been an accident?" }, { s: "Brine", t: "\"A pinned valve and a loosened joint. The soot in the burner says the flame died for want of air. Then the pinned valve kept pouring raw gas through the dead burner. Either fault alone might have left him a headache. Together, Inspector, they are a recipe.\"" } ] : [ { y: "Could it have been an accident?" }, { s: "Brine", t: "\"Coal-gas doesn't leak from a sound lamp. If you've looked at the lamp, tell me what you saw.\"" } ]

beats.t: "Apoplexy. I'd rather he had been less certain. A physician who smells gas and says apoplexy is not a physician I would quote."

objects.label: Take samples to the laboratory
objects.intro: You lay out the four samples on Brine's bench: wax, shim, cake and wrench.

lockedBeats.t: "I can tell you a great deal, but I need the wax from the bracket, the shim from the valve, a scraping from that pantry cake, and the wrench's jaws. Bring me those, and I'll bring you an answer."

beats.n: The Chief Constable comes down in a fur-collared coat, having clearly been fetched from his bed and not forgiven the fact.

beats.t: "Well, Hale? Apoplexy, I understand. A great man, a great strain. I'd like the file closed by breakfast."
"The doctor says a good many things. A murder at the Lamplighting Gala. Do you know what the Guild will say? Have your answer by morning, Hale, and have it be a quiet one."

lampworks.name: Vennard Lampworks, Cinder Row
lampworks.recap: Cinder Row is dark but for the gatehouse lamp. The furnaces tick as they cool.

objects.label: Ask Old Dunstan for the gate ledger
Examine the personnel book in the office

infirmary.name: Quillon Infirmary, Ashlar Street
infirmary.recap: The infirmary is hushed and smells of carbolic. Nurse Coll watches you from the night desk.

objects.label: Examine the appointment book; ask Nurse Coll

tinkers.name: Tinkers' Row Workshop
tinkers.recap: The workshop is cold. The gale rattles the brass signs in the lane outside.

objects.label: Examine the papers on the bench

wire.name: The Wire-Office
wire.recap: The keys chatter on. Mr. Amberley waits at his counter, proud of his filing.

objects.label: Ask for wires to Vennard House
Ask Mr. Amberley what he remembers
Ask about wires to Mr. Corvane

records.name: The Hall of Records
records.recap: The green lamp burns on. Miss Thorne looks up over her steel spectacles.

objects.label: Ask Miss Thorne about Commissioner Loam

lockedText.lampworks: You have no reason to go there yet. Perhaps the laboratory will give you one.
